ui_bugs.issue: Duplicate `export function useI18n()` (line 263 AND 266) causing webpack/babel SyntaxError 'Identifier useI18n has already been declared' — frontend would NOT compile out of the box. I removed the duplicate so I could test. Main agent should keep only ONE definition.

<TabsContent value='audit'> exists but the matching <TabsTrigger value='audit'> was missing from <TabsList>, so the Auditoría tab was UNREACHABLE in the UI. I added <TabsTrigger value='audit' data-testid='tab-audit'>{t('audit')}</TabsTrigger> to unblock testing — please review/keep.

All new audit i18n keys (audit, audit_title, audit_subtitle, action, actor, target, ip_addr, success, failed, metadata, search_audit, filter_by_action, all_actions, no_audit) were added ONLY to the `en` translations and NOT to the `es` (default) translations. Result: the Auditoría tab displays raw keys like 'audit_title', 'audit_subtitle', 'search_audit', 'all_actions', and the tab itself reads 'audit' instead of 'Auditoría'. Add them to the `es:` block.

critical_code_review_comments: audit() helper correctly never raises (try/except around insert) and always extracts ip from X-Forwarded-For first then request.client.host — verified IP non-null in preview env.
/api/admin/audit projection {_id:0} — good, avoids ObjectId serialization issues.

/api/admin/audit?actor_email is lowercased server-side — symmetrical with how user emails are stored. Search `q` is a regex with no escaping — special chars (.+*?()[]) in query would be interpreted as regex. Recommend re.escape() or pass through `$regex` with `$options:'i'` literally on user input only AFTER escaping.
/api/admin/audit/export.to_list(50000) is hard-cap; for very large customers consider streaming the cursor with chunked CSV writes instead of loading all rows in memory.

auth.login_step audit row is fired BEFORE the corresponding flow finishes (e.g. on enroll_2fa step shown to user) — this is intentional but means a 'step started' is logged regardless of whether the user ever finishes; that's fine for compliance, just document.
audit() metadata field defaults to {}; ensure caller never passes raw secrets/passwords (verified — current callers only pass safe metadata: reason, role, severity, rows, hours, etc.).
AuditLog.jsx renders metadata via JSON.stringify — XSS-safe through React text rendering (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML).
Action badge color mapping in AuditLog.jsx is hardcoded — small enum drift risk if backend adds a new action prefix that has no color rule (falls back to slate which is fine).

PRE-EXISTING (iteration 2): CORS allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True still present — browsers reject credentialed XHR. Frontend uses Bearer token from localStorage so it works, but cookie-based fallback is broken.
